title: Explainable machine learning model diagnoses vascular depression in older adults
summary: A LightGBM model with SHAP-based feature reduction was developed in 602 participants (236 vascular depression patients, 366 controls) and kept 8 features, including white matter hyperintensity score, age, VEGF, IL-6, BDNF, TNF-alpha, lacune counts and serotonin level. AUROC was 0.937 internally and 0.896 in an external set of 171 participants, marginally exceeding clinician-level performance. The design is case-control.
ai_technology: LightGBM selected among six algorithms, with SHAP interpretation

evidence.tested: Cross-validation and internal validation, with an independent external set of 171 participants from surrounding areas.
evidence.unknown: Performance in prospective, general-clinic populations; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Combines clinical, neuropsychological, blood and MRI features to classify vascular depression.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
